answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making standing a living record: every identity keeps a public, append-only history of verified useful work, a lotus that must keep growing or it sinks. Each epoch, independent peers anchor a random sample of that history by re-checking it, and any gap or forgery resets the record to zero. Fakes drain away like water through karst: each one needs its own full, genuine history, so the farm's cost grows with every fake while the reward is split among them.
